chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"Allah did not send a prophet at any time except that, in Allah's knowledge, when He completed his religion, prohibition of wine (khamr) was included in it. And wine remained forbidden; indeed, the religion is that it is transferred from one characteristic (stage) to another. And if it had been that all at once, it would have been cut off from them before the religion [was fully established]."

key_terms.قُطِعَ بِهِمْ: It was cut off from them

ai.seo_question: What is the theological explanation for the gradual prohibition of wine in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elucidates the concept of *tadrij* (gradualism) in divine legislation, asserting that while wine was eternally forbidden in Allah's knowledge, its prohibition was revealed incrementally to accommodate human nature. This scholarly insight highlights that the religion is built upon progressive adaptation rather than abrupt imposition, ensuring the message remains accessible and sustainable for the community.
